Subject: Follow-up: AWS Marketplace private offer economics & target $/1M tokens

Hi Priya / AWS team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same frame for the private offer mapping. High level: Acme is targeting a private-offer billing arrangement on AWS so your product is purchased through the AWS Marketplace but invoiced/paid via AWS. The core ask for today was: map token-based unit economics to an AWS PO SKU and confirm target $/1M tokens that hits Acme's budget.

Key items we discussed:
- Monthly token profile: 300M peak / 75M avg over initial 12 months (Priya confirmed this rough shape).
- Target unit economics: Acme is aiming for ~$1,200 per 1M tokens to match blended budget targets for early production.
- Commitment tiers: suggested REDWOOD list -> 0-1B, 1B-5B, 5B+ with incremental discounts (we discussed 10% @ 1B, 20% @ 5B).
- Marketplace mapping: need an AWS SKU that supports per-1M token metering or an equivalent consumption metric; otherwise use a fixed monthly unit tied to forecasted bundles with reconciliation.

Action items / next steps (owners):
1) Alex: share a PO draft that maps the 1M-token unit to an AWS SKU and includes the three commitment tiers (attached: po_draft_acme_redwood_v1.pdf).
2) Ben: run a quick margin check on the proposed $1,200/1M tokens across the expected mix (300M peak / 75M avg) and flag any shortfalls.
3) Priya: confirm whether Acme can accept a tiered private offer (commit -> discounted PPU) and whether legal needs a specific clause for metering reconciliation.
4) AWS: confirm marketplace SKU options for metered billing and whether they support per-1M granularity or only per-request/second metering.

I've attached a simple mapping workbook (ppu_mapping_acme_aws.xlsx) with a sample conversion from tokens -> hourly RUs -> SKU quantity (one tab for metered SKU approach, one for bundle approach). Please review and comment directly in the Drive link.

Proposed follow-up: 45-minute sync next Tue (Aug 18) to lock down SKU path and finalize the private offer draft. If that works for everyone, I'll send a calendar invite.

Alex — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the workbook: 

- The 300M peak figure is our estimate for Q1 go-live; our safer baseline for contracting is 60-80M/mo (we used 75M avg as you noted).
- On unit economics: $1,200/1M tokens is within range if we get a ~15% marketplace concession on top of Redwood list. If AWS takes >10% fee on the private offer routing, we need to reflect that in the PO so Redwood receives net ~$1,020/1M.
- We are open to a tiered commit model. Prefer a 12-month commit with quarterly true-ups rather than monthly.

Questions for AWS: can we structure the private offer so the seller (Redwood) sets the meter pricing and AWS remits on gross less marketplace fee? Also need to confirm how overage billing works in private offers.

I'll confirm with Legal on the reconciliation language — I expect a short addendum request. I'll also try to pull a draft of our procurement timeline and share it by EOD Thursday.

Hi all — quick notes from Marketplace ops:

- Metering granularity: AWS metered billing supports per-unit metering, but the unit must be defined at SKU creation. If you want "per 1M tokens" as the SKU unit, we can create a custom usage dimension named TOKEN_1M and set that as the metering dimension. That will show up as quantity on the customer's usage report.
- Fees & settlement: AWS takes a standard marketplace fee on gross; seller receives payout net of that fee. Private offers do not change marketplace fee mechanics — they only change negotiated price seen by buyer. For your arithmetic, assume 5-12% fee range depending on seller enrollment and programs.
- Overage handling: private offers can be configured with auto-invoice for overage or with manual true-up. Quarterly true-ups are fully supported but must be included in the contract terms.

Next steps from AWS side: we'll provision a draft SKU with TOKEN_1M as a test dimension and share the SKU id by end of day tomorrow. We'll also add notes on settlement timing so Acme can align cashflow.

Regards,
